tossups.text: J.R.R. Tolkien may have named the Green Dragon Inn after a bar in this novel called the Green Dragon, where several characters run up debts gambling on pool. A character in this novel allows a seriously ill alcoholic access to his brandy, knowing that the liquor will likely kill him. Its prelude claims that, while Saint Teresa led a life of greatness, there are many people who are just as good but never have the chance to achieve fame. A character in this novel burns the second will of Mr. Featherstone. Because he made his fortune pawning stolen goods, a banker in this book is blackmailed by John Raffles. It includes the story of Edward Casaubon, whose will denies his wife her inheritance if she gets remarried to Will Ladislaw. For 10 points, name this novel titled for an English town by George Eliot.

This poem was written under the pen-name Glirastes a few weeks before Horace Smith wrote that "some Hunter may express / wonder like ours" in another poem on the same subject, inspired by a passage in Diodorus Siculus. This poem mentions "lifeless things" whose record of passions survives "the heart that fed," as well as "The hand that mocked them." Smith's version focuses on "a gigantic Leg," while this poem mentions a "wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command," and "Two vast and trunkless legs of stone." For 10 points name this poem describing the wreck of an Egyptian statue, written by Percy Shelley.

Polydectes ["polly"-dek-teez] ordered the death of this figure, whose blood formed coral reefs when it fell into the sea. This sister of Stheno [s-theh-noh] and Euryale [yoo-ree-ah-lee] was punished for defiling Athena's temple with Poseidon, and her face was pressed into Athena's Aegis [ee-jiss] shield. Perseus used another shield as a mirror to help avoid this woman's petrifying gaze. For 10 points, name this gorgon, who turned humans to stone with her terrifying face and snake hair.

This quantity equals four pi times a length scale times Avogadro's number times an effective diffusion constant for diffusion-controlled processes. The steric factor equals an experimental value for this quantity divided by a value predicted from collision theory. The natural logarithm of this quantity equals "minus activation energy over quantity R times temperature." The units of this quantity depend on the reaction's order. The temperature dependence of this quantity is given by the Arrhenius ("uh-REE-nee-us") equation. For 10 points, name this constant that describes the "speed" at which a reaction proceeds.

One meal consumed during this holiday begins with eating a date and is called iftar. During this period, the beginning of the day is defined as the moment at which a human eye can tell the difference between black and white threads. The Night of Power during this period celebrates the Quran first being revealed to Muhammad by Jibril. For 10 points, name this ninth month of the Islamic calendar, during which Muslims fast from dawn to dusk.

The Rhenish missionary Pardey and Corporal John were active in converting these people to Christianity. As part of the Otruppe movement, these people westernized their communities into military districts. These people appealed to Courtney Clarke to lower the price of bone meal from 26 cents after their cattle were plagued with botulism. Since 1923, these people have celebrated Red Flag Day in Okahandja to honor the body of one of their leaders. According to EugenFischer, these people's women were forced to boil the skulls of their inmates while being detained at Shark Island. In one war, these people allied with the rival chieftain Hendrik Witbooi. After Lothar von Trotha defeated Samuel Maharero at the Battle of Waterberg, he issued a famous extermination order against these people. The Germans committed a genocide against, for 10 points, what natives of Namibia?

This thinker opened a book by asking why we value truths, rather than untruths, in a section titled "On The Prejudices of the Philosophers." This thinker popularized the idea that we will infinitely relive each moment of our lives in exactly the same way. He argued that Jews have a morality which prizes humility, whereas Romans prized power, to explain the difference between master and slave. This philosopher of a "will to power" also theorized a "superman" called Ubermensch in a book about Zarathustra. For 10 points, name this nihilistic German philosopher who claimed that "God is dead."

Garbage collection can be used to mitigate the effects of one form of this error which occurs when there is not enough contiguous space to satisfy a memory allocation call. A call graph can be used to debug instances of this error which arise from infinite recursion or unintended cyclic calls which consume more memory than is available. The handling of this phenomenon in C causes undefined behavior for signed integers and wrapping around for unsigned integers. This error's integer form occurs when a value cannot be represented using the given number of bits. For 10 points, name this error whose "stack" form shares a name with a popular online knowledge base.

John Mearshimer preaches an "offensive" version, and Reinhold Neibuhr had a Christian variety. Among its followers in American government were Kennan, Kissinger, and Scowcroft. Kenneth Waltz attempted to combine it with structuralist thinking to create a more rigorous program of political research, but its proponents have been reluctant to incorporate game theory into their writings. It insists that states are the only actors who play a significant role in world politics, the international system is anarchical, and that states are unitary rational actors motivated by survival. For 10 points name this broad, often pessimistic school of international relations theorists such as Hans Morgenthau and E.H. Carr, contrasted in IR theory with liberalism, though the term is usually opposed to idealism in philosophy.

This man's final symphony was completed by Deryck Cooke. This man depicted a child's vision of heaven in the song "Das himmlische Leben," which he included in his Fourth Symphony. Another symphony by this man includes the text of a Klopstock poem that begins "Rise again, yes, rise again," while another symphony by this man is based on the hymn "Veni Creator Spiritus." This man used text from poems by Friedrich Rückert and Li Po in his Kindertotenlieder and his The Song of the Earth, respectively. For 10 points, name this Austrian composer of the "Resurrection" Symphony and The Symphony of a Thousand.

In the hot chocolate effect, this quantity is reduced because of bubble density, which occurs due to the addition of fine powders to liquids. The mass specific total enthalpy in perfect gas compressible flow is equal to a term featuring this quantity squared multiplied by quantity one plus partial derivative of pressure with respect to energy multiplied by M squared, end quantity. For an ideal gas, this is given by the square root of the adiabatic index times pressure divided by density, and it is generally given by the square root of the bulk modulus divided by density. Generally approximated as 331 meters per second in dry air at 0 Celsius, the speed of an object divided by this quantity is known as the Mach number. For 10 points, name this quantity defined as the rate at which waves that transfer noise move through an elastic medium.

this structure is essential for feedback loops. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in feedback loops.

tossups.text: John Bidwell, a farmer, wrote an account of life before and after this event. Because of this event, one man was unable to start his dream of creating the agricultural empire of New Helvetica. It was brought to the public's attention after publisher Samuel Brennan ran through the streets shouting about the American River. People who participated in this event were called Argonauts, and could either round Cape Horn, go through disease infested Panama or use the same trail that the Donner Party used. This event began when James Marshall made a discovery at Sutter's Mill. For 10 points, name this event that began in 1849, which saw many prospectors travel to a certain western state in search of fortune.
acceptableAnswers: the discovery of gold in California

tossups.text: A character in this poem prophecies that "Thou shalt prove how salt is the taste of another man's bread and how hard is the way up and down another man's stairs." In this poem, Justinian summarizes the glorious episodes of Roman history and laments the present era by comparison. In this poem's eighteenth canto, the final letter of the Latin phrase "QUI IUDICATIS TERRAM" transforms into a giant eagle. At the very end of this poem, the protagonist is stirred by "the Love which moves the sun and the other stars," while trying to conceptualize how three concentric circles represent the trinity. St. Bernard prays to Mary on behalf of the protagonist of this poem after he sees an enormous rose housing several souls, in a plane beyond physical existence known as the Empyrean. In this poem, the Moon and Mercury are among the nine spheres of the title realm through which the protagonist is guided by his beloved, Beatrice. For 10 points, name this final part of Dante's Divine Comedy.

This river's native baiji was the first species of dolphin to have a human-caused extinction. Over 1 million people were displaced by the construction of the Three Gorges Dam on this river, which is connected to another river to its north by the Grand Canal. This river is located south of the Yellow River and has its mouth near Shanghai. For 10 points, name this longest river in China.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for thymus gland. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this lymph-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The lymph is a key component of the Immune system, involved in thymus gland.

tossups.text: This novel's protagonist uses a "green bullet" to communicate with Faber. This novel's protagonist reads "Dover Beach" while surrounded by television parlor walls, and memorizes the Book of Ecclesiastes. A stomach pump is used to treat the morphine-addicted Mildred in this novel. A mechanical hound in this novel is melted while inecting anesthetics. Captain Beatty leads book-burning "firemen" in, for ten points, what Ray Bradbury novel about Guy Montag?

This man's "first law" states that objects uninfluenced by forces move along geodesic curves. Inertial and gravitational mass equal each other according to this scientist's equivalence principle. The metric tensor and cosmological constant appear in a set of field equations developed by this scientist to describe gravity. Gravitational lensing is a consequence of a theory of this scientist that defines gravity as the result of curvature of spacetime. For 10 points, name this scientist, who developed "general" and "special" theories of relativity.

Vasopressin inserts aquaporins into sections of this organ to regulate blood pressure. A concentration gradient is created by reabsorbing ions through this organ's Loop of Henle. The Bowman's capsule encloses this organ's filtering portion, the glomerulus, at the beginning of its functional unit, called a nephron. Dialysis is used after this organ fails. For 10 points, name this bean- shaped organ that filters blood and concentrates urine.

this structure is essential for systemic circulation. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this systole-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The systole is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in systemic circulation.

parts.text: Name this 1786 comedy that also features Clifford pursuing Emily Gayville.
Like The Maid of the Oaks, The Heiress is a play by this British author, who may be better known for losing the Battle of Saratoga.
The title character, Dick Dudgeon, is condemned by Anthony Anderson and pardoned by John Burgoyne in this only George Bernard Shaw play with an American setting.

bonuses.leadin: Adapted from Charlotte Lenox's The Sister and Denis Diderot's Father of the Family, this play ends with Miss Alton finding out that she is the true claimant to the fortune of Miss Alscrip. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Civil War battle of 1864, a bloody stalemate fought by Grant and Meade at the start of the Overland campaign.

After the Civil War, a murder in Lambeth, and imprisonment in Broadmoor for insanity, William Chester Minor produced his most famous work on this project. James Murray and Herbert Coleridge both led this extensive philological project at various points.

This English author contributed definitions for the Oxford English dictionary in the range near the word "waggle" including most famously for the word "walrus". This man is credited with popularizing the words orc and mithril which now appear in the dictionary.

bonuses.leadin: William Chester Minor apparently branded the face of a deserter with a letter D following this battle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process in the Egyptian afterlife, where one of the subject's organs is compared against the feather of Maat.
The weighing of the heart is overseen by this jackal-headed Egyptian god of the afterlife, who also presides over the mummification process.
Ammit, the devourer of souls, has the head of one of these reptiles, whose snout shape differentiates them from alligators.

bonuses.leadin: At the end of this process, the subject either continues to the Field of Reeds or their soul is devoured by Ammit. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this polyatomic anion produced by the complete dissociation of H2SO4.

To form Lindlar's catalyst, barium sulfate and quinone are added to palladium to accomplish this. This is the term for reducing the activity of a catalyst by adding substances that bind to its active sites.
A ruthenium carbene catalyst developed by Grubbs is used to carry out this process, the switching of double bonds from one alkene to another.

bonuses.leadin: This compound bonded to copper is used in a solution to test for the presence of reducing sugars, Benedict's reagent. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Mencius and Zengzi helped record the works of this major Chinese thinker, the namesake of a Chinese philosophical system.
Written by his students, this representative collection of Confucian sayings was finished during the Warring States Period.
Popular in the Qin [CHIN] dynasty, this other philosophy espoused by Qin Shi Huang-di's brutality led to the rise of religions like Confucianism.

bonuses.leadin: He believed in five fundamental relationships, and the concept of jen, a reflection of one's goodness. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The sinking of the HMS Sheffield and the merchant ship Atlantic Conveyor occurred during this 1982 war between Argentina and the United Kingdom over an archipelago off Argentina's coast.

The USS Stark was sunk during this 1980-1988 conflict, which occurred after the Islamic revolution in one country. It was sparked by an assassination attempt on Tariq Aziz and partly fought for control of the Shatt al-Arab waterway.
Both the USS Stark and the Atlantic Conveyor were sunk by these French-developed anti-ship missiles, which take their name from flying fish. Its name entered British slang during the Falklands war.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some things about ships sinking or getting sunk in recent history, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Esther and her uncle Mordecai (MOR-duh-kai) enter the court of Ahasuerus (ay-HAS-oo-EHR-uhs) and stop a genocide, which Jews commemorate on this holiday.
Shushan Purim is celebrated in this city's Safar Square. King Solomon built the First Temple in this holiest Jewish city.
During Purim, children shake these noisemakers while the Megillah (muh-GILL-uh) is recited. These objects drown out the name of Haman (HAA-maan), who hangs on the gallows that he constructed.

bonuses.leadin: A fast preceding this holiday commemorates Esther fasting for three days with her seven maids. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this statement, an upper mass limit for white dwarf stars. It is named for an Indian astrophysicist.
Within one-tenth, this is the maximum number of solar masses that a white dwarf may attain before experiencing gravitational collapse, according to the Chandrasekhar limit.

As a consequence of the Chandrasekhar limit, stars in this region of the HR diagram will become either neutron stars or black holes once they are at or above 8 solar masses. The sun is in this region of the HR diagram.

bonuses.leadin: Tolman, Oppenheimer, and Volkoff name an analogous version of this statement for neutron stars. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Different languages have different rules for how these three things should be arranged in a sentence. These things represent the action being taken in a sentence, the thing doing the action, and the thing the action is being done to.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on VSO in any order

parts.text: This is the verb-subject-object ordering in English and Mandarin.
The least common ordering, object-subject-verb, is mostly found in languages in this region. A controversial 2005 paper claimed that a language from this region lacked recursion.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the order of words in a sentence, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this two-word term coined by Wesleyan University professor Robert Brown in the 1960s. It generally refers to the products of folk traditions.

The World Music Institute organizes performances by female examples of these poets from Central Asia, whom they bill as "divas." Celtic examples of these people composed music to accompany their epic stories.
Other WMI shows have featured shira songs composed by these people in Yemen. In Europe, these people developed klezmer music.

bonuses.leadin: An "institute" named for this sort of art partners with New York City concert halls to perform theyyam dances from Kerala, Laotian poetry, and other diverse forms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this property which describes the direction of oscillation of light.

Circularly polarized light is formed by superimposing waves with perpendicular polarization and which differ in this quantity. The quotient of angular frequency and wavenumber gives this quantity's "velocity."
The phase lag of pi over two required to produce circularly polarized light can be produced when linearly polarized light passes through the "fast" and "slow" axes of these devices.

bonuses.leadin: This property for light can be represented with a Jones vector. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with capillary exchange.
What is the main function of the aorta in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to capillary exchange.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Though this man successfully wrangled Egyptian concessions and planned the building of the Suez Canal, his involvement in Panama was a debacle which ended with his conviction for defrauding investors and bribing politicians.

Georges Picquart, Emile Zola, and Georges Clemenceau were among those who pointed out that Major Esterhazy, not this Jewish captain, was responsible for selling military secrets to the Germans in 1894.

The Panama Scandal, the picaresque intrigues of George Boulanger, and labor unrest all raged during the 1887 to 1894 presidency of this man, whose last indignity was his assassination by the anarchist Sante Caserio.

bonuses.leadin: The French Third Republic was best by a series of political scandals in the late nineteenth century. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This author of Konrad Wallenrod and Forefathers Eve wrote the Polish national epic, Pan Tadeusz.
This author of Children of the Soil and Without Dogma used Rome under Nero as the setting for his Christian novel Quo Vadis.
This realist writer may be best known for such stories as The Barrel-Organ and The Doll, though he also wrote The Emancipated Women and A Legend of Old Egypt.

bonuses.leadin: Name these Polish authors, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name these primates whose most widely recognized species is the "ring-tailed" one. This primate is endemic to an island also home to most species of the baobab tree and the Malagasy people.
Lemurs are endemic to this extremely biodiverse island nation, separated from mainland Africa by the Mozambique Channel.
Lemurs are the only primates other than humans to possess blue features in these organs. Lemurs possess large examples of these organs, allowing them to see well at night.

bonuses.leadin: The Aye-Aye species of this primate is the largest nocturnal primate in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with heart valves and their functions.
What is the main function of the atrium in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to heart valves and their functions.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: This is what novel in which the police inspector Javert pursues the protagonist, who has adopted the name Father Madeleine?
This protagonist of Les Miserables is released from prison, but cannot succeed in society because he is branded as a convict by his yellow passport.
This author of Toilers of the Sea and The Hunchback of Notre Dame wrote Les Miserables.

bonuses.leadin: Fantine befriends the protagonist who seeks advice from the Bishop of Digne. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this laboratory procedure that can be used to find the concentration of an acid.
Weak acids are titrated with strong types of this substance. Examples include sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide.
This indicator is used for a weak acid-strong base titration. It is clear in an acidic environment but turns pink in a basic environment.

bonuses.leadin: This procedure is used to create a namesake curve on which the equivalence point lies. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these entities. This tournament is almost surely taking place in the Milky Way, one of these astronomical objects which contains the Solar System.
The Milky Way will eventually collide with this closest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way. It is named after the mythological wife of Perseus.
The Andromeda Galaxy is one entry in the Messier catalog, whose first entry is a nebula named for this animal. The constellation Cancer is named for its supposed resemblance to one of these animals.

bonuses.leadin: The Hubble tuning fork can be used to classify these entities. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with spinal cord structure.
What is the main function of the spinal cord in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to spinal cord structure.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.
